items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I took Edgar Courance who was still playing C melody sax, William Smith on piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto and Edgar James, drums.

ctx.x: The first out of town job came not long after we had finished at the Pekin Theatre. A fellow came from Richmond, Indiana and engaged the Maycock group to play a dance there. When the date came this fellow sent a car to bring us to Richmond. There we got as much food as we could eat, plenty of drinks and we made a big hit with the dancers.

Two weeks later we went back to Richmond and then the organizer told me that he would like me to be the leader of the orchestra the next time they had a dance. There was one about three weeks after that and I took Edgar Courance who was still playing C melody sax, William Smith on piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto and Edgar James, drums.

When we arrived in Richmond and I saw the advertising bills and posters for the dance, I wasn't happy about the way they had been made. There was the name of the hall and the date of the dance and in big letters "Professor Johnson Coleman" and his band. I did not like the idea of me being called "Professor" because my idea of professor was an older person than I was and in the case of being a musician, a professor was one that knew all about music and was also a music teacher.
